title: Differentiating an Accumulation Function with Chain Rule
originalTopic: Leibniz Rule / Chain Rule with FTC 1
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the derivative with respect to x of G(x) = int_0^{x^2} cos(t^2) dt.

steps.title: Define Composite Form
steps.mathExpression: G(x) = F(u(x)), \quad u(x) = x^2, \quad F(u) = \int_0^u \cos(t^2) dt
steps.explanation: Identify the upper limit as a composite function u(x) = x^2.

steps.title: Differentiate Outer and Inner Functions
steps.explanation: FTC Part 1 yields F'(u), standard power rule yields u'(x).

steps.title: Combine via Chain Rule
steps.explanation: Multiply outer derivative by inner derivative.
steps.why: Chain Rule application to integral functions.
